changelog.title: Project site
items: Configs, Stats, Setup and About pages; a launch link and a config file for the local game.
Save backups are read in the browser; nothing is uploaded.

changelog.title: Free Ride
items: Starts an endless freestyle session in the stadium arena, with the intro movies skipped.
Optionally stops at the rider and ATV choice on the way in.

changelog.title: Local start page
items: A start page for the local game with Play and Free Ride, settings (display, movies, volume, controls, settings as text), saves, game data and a changelog.
A menu over the game on F1 or Esc: FPS counter, fullscreen, screenshot, settings, log download, quit.
Keyboard keys and gamepad buttons can be rebound.

changelog.title: Your own game folder
items: The local page asks for the folder of your own USA copy, checks default.xbe, and copies the files into the browser's private storage once.
An interrupted copy resumes. Removing the game files keeps the saves.
The local server sends no game data of its own.

changelog.title: Saves
items: Saves persist in the browser and export to a zip in the Windows build's folder layout; the Windows save folder can be imported back.
Imports are checked first and the previous saves are kept as a backup.

changelog.title: Display options
items: Internal resolution 1x to 8x or matched to the window, MSAA, and the game's own 16:9 mode.
Split-screen views are scaled with the resolution.

changelog.title: Split screen
items: Two to four players, each on their own gamepad, on Windows and in the browser.
Four-player Windows runs went from about 35 to 60 fps after the GPU command walk and vertex handling were fixed.

changelog.title: A race at 60 fps in Edge
items: Races hold 60 fps in the browser; without the frame cap about 116.
Keyboard and gamepad drive player 1.

changelog.title: Sound and movie skip
items: Sound plays in the browser through an AudioWorklet after the first click or key.
Skipping the movies reaches the title screen in under 15 seconds.
A mixing bug that made the left channel louder and clip is fixed.

changelog.title: WebGPU
items: The GPU work is recorded as frame packets and drawn with WebGPU; the console's vertex programs and pixel combiners become WGSL shaders.
Guest memory and hardware registers work without page faults, which WebAssembly does not have.

changelog.title: GPU renderer
items: First GPU-drawn frames, then vertex programs and combiners on the GPU, then a full race at full speed.
Mipmaps, tyres and a black-square texture bug fixed.

changelog.title: Static recompile
items: The retail Xbox game translated to C with an open-source static recompiler and running on Windows: menus, races and movies.

milestones.title: Boots on Windows
milestones.text: The recompiled game reaches its intro movies, title screen, menus and a race. Two runtime fixes were needed: the USB controller setup was never called, and a watchdog timer killed healthy runs.

milestones.title: Frame packets on the GPU
milestones.text: Instead of drawing pixels on the CPU, the console's GPU commands are recorded as packets and replayed on a real GPU, with shaders generated from the console's vertex programs and pixel combiners.

milestones.title: A full race at 60 fps
milestones.text: A software interrupt and a faster command kick-off let the game and the GPU run side by side; the first complete race at full speed followed.

milestones.title: WebAssembly and WebGPU
milestones.text: The same C builds for WebAssembly. One web worker per game thread, the game's files from the browser's private storage, sound through an AudioWorklet, graphics through WebGPU.

milestones.title: Play from your own disc
milestones.text: The browser page asks for the player's own game folder, verifies it, and keeps a private copy. The local server never serves game data.

milestones.title: Polish
milestones.text: Saves, display options, split screen, Free Ride, a start page, smoother race starts and cleaner sound.
